Probably not.

Although the Moon is geometrically above the horizon, it is only an **11.4%-illuminated waning crescent** and just **39.4° from the Sun**. In bright daylight its illuminated portion has low contrast against the blue sky. Its altitude of **18.2°** also means extra atmospheric scattering and extinction, further reducing visibility.

Under exceptionally transparent conditions, an experienced observer who knows the exact position might possibly detect it, especially with binoculars—but for an ordinary observer using unaided eyesight, even with clear skies, it would be **very difficult and likely invisible**.

So you can reasonably expect **not to be able to spot it**, though visibility cannot be ruled out completely. Avoid sweeping near the Sun with binoculars or a telescope.
